name: SNAP Application Assistance
provider: The Food Bank of Western Massachusetts
description: The Food Bank's SNAP outreach team can check whether you may be eligible for SNAP and help you apply by phone, online, or in person. Eligibility for SNAP itself is determined by the Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA).
contact: Food Bank SNAP line 413-992-6204; Food Bank 413-247-9738 or 888-792-4523

requirements.text: The Food Bank's SNAP help is free to all Western Massachusetts residents (the Food Bank serves Hampden, Hampshire, Berkshire, and Franklin Counties).

The Food Bank's page lists SNAP gross monthly income limits by household size (add $947 for each member beyond 8). Meeting these limits does not mean you are definitely eligible; DTA makes the decision.
SNAP eligibility is determined by the Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA) based on household size, composition, income, and expenses.

guide.what: Monthly money for groceries. The Food Bank's SNAP team checks whether you may qualify and helps you apply for free.
guide.decided_by: The Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA) decides. The Food Bank helps you apply

ways.title: Call the Food Bank
ways.detail: SNAP line 413-992-6204. They can apply with you over the phone.

ways.title: Send a referral online
ways.detail: Fill out a short form and the Food Bank calls you back.

ways.title: In person
ways.detail: The team also helps in person. Ask where when you call 413-247-9738.

guide.no_documents_note: The Food Bank page doesn't list SNAP documents. Ask on your first call so you can gather them before the application.
ask_them: Which documents should I have ready?
Are there limits on savings or other assets?
Which year are the income limits on your page for?

first_step.title: Apply for SNAP with free help from the Food Bank
first_step.detail: Call the Food Bank SNAP line at 413-992-6204, or send a referral online and they will call you.
